authored: This file declares the SHAPE of a format and the surprises a reader has to survive. It contains nothing taken from anybody's file. Sample files are generated from it by scripts/generate-intake-fixture.mjs, and their content is invented.
literalUse: FORMAT DISCRIMINATOR. The headings below are the strings a reader must match to recognise this format at all; they are the same ones the adapter carries. No section name, item name, comment text or rating word from any real export appears in this repository.

quirks.statement: There may be no shared-string table at all, with every value carried in the worksheet itself. The type marking those values is `str`, which the format defines as a FORMULA's string result, not `inlineStr`. A reader that recognises only `inlineStr` therefore finds no text anywhere and reports an empty sheet rather than an error.
quirks.measuredNote: Restated 2026-08-24 from what the corpus file actually contains. The earlier wording said the table 'may be empty, with every value written inline', and both halves were wrong in a way that matters: the table is ABSENT rather than empty, and the values are not inline strings.

quirks.statement: A value's text may be escaped twice, so ONE decode leaves an entity where a character belongs. Whether that reaches the reader depends on the reader: a conformant XML parser decodes exactly once and surfaces the entity, while a parser that decodes until the text stops changing resolves it by accident and shows the right character.
quirks.measuredNote: The second sentence is the important half and was added 2026-08-24 after measuring it. This deployment's parser is the second kind, so this quirk currently has NO visible consequence here — which is not the same as the file being clean, and would flip the day the parser is replaced by a conformant one.

quirks.statement: The column that classifies a row may be empty on some rows, and those rows are otherwise complete.
Parent names repeat on every row: the nesting is implied by repetition rather than expressed.

A row may omit a cell entirely rather than writing an empty one, so position in the row does not give a column. A row also carries EMPTY cells that are written as a self-closing element with no value, so both spellings of 'nothing here' occur in the same row and neither can be read positionally.
A text value may carry U+00A0 rather than an ordinary space, including at its start and end. It is not a separator to split on, and it is invisible in every view of the file a person has.
quirks.measuredNote: Added 2026-08-24. Measured, not assumed, and it was not in this schema before: nobody had looked. Confined to the comment-text column in the corpus file, so it does not affect how rows group into sections and items — but a reader that trims with a set of characters of its own rather than the language's whitespace definition would leave it on the ends of values.
